title: Bob's bit away from the special coordinate
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$ and a sample $\omega$ of the hard distribution, consisting of a distinguished coordinate $T \in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, two bits $x_T$ and $y_T$, and an assignment $i \mapsto \omega_{\text{other}}(i)$ of a disjoint coordinate-type (one of *neither*, *left only*, *right only*) to each coordinate. For every coordinate $i \ne T$, Bob's bit at $i$ under this sample equals the bit $y(\omega_{\text{other}}(i))$ read off from the coordinate-type assigned to $i$; that is, away from the distinguished coordinate the distinguished bit $y_T$ plays no role.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number
ω is a HardSample (distinguished coordinate T, bits xT and yT, coordinate-type assignment `other`)
i is a coordinate in Fin n
